permutationLabel: Non-jaundiced — age ≥60 with weight loss, back pain and new-onset diabetes (NICE NG12 urgent CT)
summary: 66-year-old woman with 7 kg weight loss over four months, a dull epigastric ache radiating to the back and diabetes diagnosed two months ago; normal LFTs, no jaundice.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Weight loss and upper abdominal ache
inputs.hpi: Lost 7 kg over four months without trying. Dull epigastric ache boring into the back, worse at night and lying flat. Diabetes diagnosed two months ago (HbA1c 8.1%), no family history of diabetes. Stools normal. No jaundice.

exam.abdomen: Mild epigastric tenderness; no mass; no hepatomegaly.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected pancreatic cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected pancreatic cancer (body/tail): age ≥60 with weight loss, back pain and new-onset diabetes — NICE NG12 urgent direct-access CT within 2 weeks.

mustNotMiss.note: NICE NG12 names exactly this combination (≥60, weight loss, back/abdominal pain, new-onset diabetes).

emergencyLevel.note: Urgent (2-week) CT; must not be booked routinely. iOS (predicted, not observed): priority — "weight loss" in the CC.

mustInclude.note: NICE NG12: urgent direct-access CT (within 2 weeks), or urgent ultrasound if CT unavailable.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral (pancreatic cancer)
guideline.section: Suspected cancer pathway referral for pancreatic cancer at age ≥40 with jaundice; urgent direct-access CT (within 2 weeks) at age ≥60 with weight loss and any of diarrhoea, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or new-onset diabetes
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG12, June 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: NICE NG85 — Pancreatic cancer in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Pancreatic-protocol CT for obstructive jaundice with suspected pancreatic cancer; EUS with tissue sampling if unclear; specialist pancreatic MDT; pre-operative biliary drainage only when surgery is delayed, for cholangitis, or before neoadjuvant therapy; SEMS for palliative biliary drainage
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NICE guideline NG85, February 2018.

rationale: Permutation: the early, non-jaundiced presentation that is most often missed. NICE NG12 gives an explicit trigger (age ≥60, weight loss plus back pain or new-onset diabetes) for urgent CT.
